statement: Direct C-source extraction of codebase-memory-mcp (DeusData, v0.8.1) surfaced two corrections to the prior x06-source-scout-digests.md §1 summary: (1) search_graph's BM25 label-boost table is Function/Method=+10.0, Route=+8.0, Class/Interface/Type/Enum=+5.0 (the digest said only 'Class' for the +5 tier, but it is actually 4 labels: Class, Interface, Type, Enum) -- src/mcp/mcp.c:1694-1700. (2) the digest claimed semantic search has 'NO neural model', but codebase-memory-mcp's own docs/llms.txt states semantic search uses bundled nomic-embed-code embeddings (768-dim, compiled into the binary) as one of 11 combined signals -- the search_graph semantic_query mode specifically implements a token-vector cosine scheme (min-cosine across keywords, not average) with a deterministic sparse-random-projection fallback for out-of-vocabulary tokens (store.c:6160-6289), but whether the token_vectors table itself is populated by the neural embedding model or a separate lexical pass was not traced in this pass -- flagged UNVERIFIED in x06-baseline-tool-schemas.md.
why: Implementers building enforcer-memory's search_graph parity would silently under-boost Interface/Type/Enum nodes and would wrongly assume semantic_query is pure-lexical (skipping neural-embedding parity work) if they trusted the digest summary over the actual C source.
howToApply: When implementing X06.4 search_graph BM25 boosting, use the 4-label +5.0 tier (Class/Interface/Type/Enum) not just Class. When implementing semantic_query parity, first resolve the UNVERIFIED token_vectors provenance question (read codebase-memory-mcp's embedding/semantic indexing pass source) before deciding whether enforcer-memory's dense retrieval stack needs to match a neural signal or can stay pure-lexical for this specific tool.

evidence.ref: codebase-memory-mcp (DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp, shallow clone) src/mcp/mcp.c:1694-1700, docs/llms.txt, src/store/store.c:6160-6289

statement: x06-baseline-tool-schemas.md was checkpointed and pushed after 7 of the 14 codebase-memory-mcp MCP tools were fully extracted and cited to file:line (query_graph, trace_path, get_code_snippet, get_architecture, search_code, search_graph, get_graph_schema) plus the shared JSON-RPC envelope, stderr logging contract, and query_graph's Cypher grammar/100k-ceiling/complexity-property details -- all via 4 parallel general-purpose research sub-agents reading the actual C source in a scratchpad clone. The remaining 7 tools (index_repository, list_projects, delete_project, index_status, detect_changes, manage_adr, ingest_traces) plus the CLI-form exit-code details and the common cross-tool error-shape confirmation are marked UNVERIFIED in sections 9-16 of the doc rather than filled from the prior scout digest's summary, per the 'never guess silently' instruction, because the 4th parallel sub-agent covering that cluster had not returned a report by the time the 7-tool checkpoint threshold was reached.
why: The task's explicit discipline required committing+pushing as soon as the first 7 tools were done rather than waiting for all 14, to create a recoverable checkpoint given the prior session assigned to this exact task died mid-work with no salvage.
howToApply: A follow-up pass (or the same lane resumed) must re-run extraction against src/mcp/mcp.c (grep index_repository/list_projects/delete_project/index_status/detect_changes/manage_adr/ingest_traces registration sites), src/mcp/index_supervisor.c, src/pipeline/pipeline.c+pipeline_incremental.c+artifact.c, src/pipeline/pass_gitdiff.c+pass_githistory.c, and src/cli/cli.c (4732 lines, never independently read in this pass) to fill sections 9-16 of x06-baseline-tool-schemas.md before it is treated as complete parity-floor grounding.
